evals.name: targeted-merged-worktree
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Clean the local allocation for merged PR #42: branch feature/export at abc123, target main, auxiliary worktree /worktrees/export. The PR head, branch tip, and clean worktree HEAD all match abc123; ignored files are verified disposable build output.
evals.expected_output: Inspect only the exact allocation, independently verify merge and current identities, remove /worktrees/export through git worktree remove from the primary repository, compare-delete local feature/export at abc123, preserve the remote branch, and verify both removals.
assertions: Targets only feature/export and /worktrees/export rather than inventorying or deleting other allocations
Requires merged PR proof, matching PR head, branch tip, worktree branch and HEAD, clean state, and reviewed ignored files
Uses registered worktree removal and expected-old-value local ref deletion
Preserves the remote branch because no remote deletion was authorized

evals.name: merge-ready-is-too-early
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. PR #51 from feature/paywall to develop is merge-ready but still open. Its auxiliary worktree is clean. Run targeted git-cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Remove nothing because merge-ready is not merged. Report cleanup pending with the exact PR state and preserve the worktree, local branch, and remote branch.
assertions: Does not treat merge-ready or green CI as merged proof
Preserves the exact branch and worktree and reports cleanup pending

evals.name: protected-branches
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. The user asks to delete local main, develop, and trunk after old PRs merged. origin/HEAD resolves to trunk.
evals.expected_output: Refuse all three deletions. Literal main and develop are permanent, and trunk is protected as the configured default branch.
assertions: Never removes main or develop
Never removes trunk because it is the configured default branch
Does not let explicit naming or merged history override protected-branch rules

evals.name: primary-checkout-switch
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Merged PR #63 used feature/settings in the primary checkout and targeted main. The checkout is clean, feature/settings still equals the verified PR head, and main exists. Describe targeted cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Switch the clean primary checkout to verified target main, re-read feature/settings, compare-delete it only at the expected PR head, preserve the remote branch, and verify the result.
assertions: Switches the primary checkout only because it is clean and the verified target is main
Rechecks branch identity and uses expected-old-value deletion
Preserves main and the remote feature branch

evals.name: broad-mode-requires-explicit-request
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Invoke git-cleanup with no branch, worktree, PR, --all, or request to clean the repository.
evals.expected_output: Request the missing target and perform no repository-wide inventory or deletion.
assertions: Does not infer permission for a broad branch or worktree sweep from a bare invocation
Deletes nothing and asks for the exact target or an explicit whole-repository request

evals.name: explicit-all-retains-global-audit
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Run git-cleanup --all --dry-run in a repository with several merged and unmerged branches and worktrees.
evals.expected_output: Inventory the whole repository, refresh remote refs when possible, classify safe, review-first, and protected candidates, and report the plan without deletion.
assertions: Uses repository-wide inventory because --all was explicit
Separates safe candidates from dirty, unique, current, shared, and protected allocations
Deletes nothing because --dry-run was supplied

evals.name: non-origin-remote-and-hierarchical-default
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Targeted cleanup concerns branch feature/api delivered to remote upstream, whose HEAD points to upstream/release/stable. The branch was not delivered to origin. Describe verification and protection.
evals.expected_output: Use the recorded upstream remote for fetch and ancestry or PR verification, preserve the full release/stable default-branch name, and refuse evidence from origin as a substitute. Never delete release/stable.
assertions: Fetches and verifies against the recorded upstream remote rather than hard-coded origin
Strips only the exact upstream/ prefix and preserves release/stable as the configured default branch
Does not delete from evidence belonging to a different remote

evals.name: primary-ignored-path-collision
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. A merged feature branch is checked out in a clean primary checkout, but ignored dev.sqlite would be tracked by target main. Describe cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Block the switch and all cleanup until dev.sqlite is preserved or explicitly disposed. A clean tracked and untracked status is insufficient because switching to main could overwrite the ignored file.
assertions: Inventories ignored paths in the primary checkout before switching
Detects the collision between ignored dev.sqlite and a tracked target path
Preserves the checkout, branch, and file while disposition is unresolved

evals.name: advanced-remote-branch-preserved
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Remote deletion of feature/api was explicitly authorized after its PR merged at abc123, but the current remote feature/api tip is def456. Describe cleanup.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the remote branch because it advanced beyond the verified PR head. A conditional expected-tip deletion must fail or be skipped; the merged state of the old PR does not authorize deleting def456.
assertions: Reads the current remote source tip immediately before deletion
Requires the remote tip to equal the verified delivered head
Uses an expected-tip lease and preserves a concurrently advanced branch

evals.name: live-default-and-fresh-target
evals.prompt: Source simulation only; execute no tools. Cached upstream/HEAD says main, but a live upstream HEAD query says refs/heads/release/stable. A custom fetch refspec leaves upstream/release/stable stale while a targeted fetch writes the current target to FETCH_HEAD. Describe cleanup verification.
evals.expected_output: Protect release/stable from the live remote HEAD result and use only the FETCH_HEAD produced by the exact target fetch for ancestry proof. Do not trust either cached remote-tracking ref.
assertions: Queries the live recorded remote HEAD and preserves the complete release/stable branch name
Does not trust cached upstream/HEAD for default-branch protection
Verifies ancestry against the FETCH_HEAD written by the exact target fetch rather than a stale remote-tracking ref
